title: Here’s What to Do Now That Microsoft Edge Is Phasing Out Ad Blockers
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 13, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Herstockart via Getty Images
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        If you're a Microsoft Edge user, you will soon find that some older extensions—like uBlock Origin—no longer work. That's because Microsoft is following Google Chrome's lead in transitioning to the Manifest V3 extensions platform and disabling MV2 add-ons in the process. Edge is built on Google's Chromium engine, so the change isn't unexpected, but it does impact users who rely on older ad blockers. Microsoft is ending support for older Edge extensionsMicrosoft recently announced that it will begin turning MV2 extensions off by default over the next few months, and support for these add-ons will end completely for most users by the close of 2026. (The transition for enterprise is expected to be finalized in early 2027.) Microsoft notes that 95% of MV2 extensions on Edge have already moved to MV3, leaving fewer than 60 in the Edge Add-on store still on MV2. That includes uBlock Origin, which does have an MV3 version in uBlock Origin Lite, but the latter isn't as powerful as its predecessor and hides content rather than keeping it from loading in the first place. AdBlock, AdBlock Plus, and AdGuard are other MV3 alternatives with Edge versions, though they are not perfect replacements for uBlock Origin either thanks to restrictions on how MV3 ad blockers are able to filter content. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
If you want to retain the ad-blocking features you're used to, you can move away from Edge (and Chrome) to a browser that's not Chromium-based. The alternatives also tend to be pretty decent when it comes to privacy. One is Firefox, which runs on its own Gecko engine and still allows these older ad-block extensions, including uBlock Origin. DuckDuckGo and Brave both have built-in ad-blocking capabilities. Note that Opera, which is Chromium-based, has said the platform plans to continue MV2 support for now, but that may end eventually.

title: You Can Score a MacBook Neo for $599 in the Middle of 'RAMageddon'
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.

            Credit: Bloomberg / Contributor via Getty Images
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        The global memory crisis—commonly referred to as RAMageddon—continues to make just about every piece of tech more expensive. Even Apple, a $4.5 trillion company, can't weather the markets without raising prices. What's more, Apple is struggling to produce enough Macs to meet demand, as you might discover if you try to buy a MacBook Air right now. While it's always a good idea to consider buying used tech, it now makes more sense than ever.As it happens, if you're in the market for Apple's "budget" Mac, the MacBook Neo, it's an excellent time to buy used. Apple originally released the MacBook Neo for $599, a fantastic price for a complete Mac experience. But since the RAM shortage, the company increased its starting price to $699—not bad, but certainly not as enticing an offer as it was at its release just five months ago. The MacBook Neo hits the Apple Refurbished Store But now, the MacBook Neo is officially available directly from Apple at its original $599 price point—as long as you buy it refurbished. But unlike buying a used piece of tech from a friend or a random outlet, Apple's refurbished store isn't unlike buying products new: The company says that it puts "Certified Refurbished" products through a "rigorous" refurbishment process, which includes testing, cleaning, and repackaging. Refurbished Apple products also have the same one-year limited warranty of new products, as well as a 14-day return policy, and you can purchase AppleCare if you so choose. As such, buying a MacBook Neo on the refurbished store should be just about the same experience as buying one new—except for the fact you have an additional $100 in your wallet. You get the same A18 Pro chip with 8GB of RAM, 13-inch display, 256GB SSD, and two USB ports (one USB 3 and one USB 2). If you want additional storage, as well as an embedded Touch ID sensor, you can upgrade to the 512GB model, also refurbished for $679.  
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
As tech gets more expensive, and companies make fewer products to sell, it makes sense to check out Apple's Refurbished Store for other devices, too. Just about every product category is represented here, to take a look before you buy a device at its full (and inflated) price.

title: Free ChatGPT Users Will Get a Huge Upgrade Next Week
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 7, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Bloomberg / Contributor via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            OpenAI is rolling out unlimited text messages for free and Go ChatGPT users next week.
                                            Free users will be able to send as many texts to ChatGPT as they want, though there will be limits on other features and messages.
                                            Plus and Pro users are also getting updates, as OpenAI is rolling out upgrades to its GPT-5.6 Sol model.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        There are 8.3 billion people on this planet, and roughly an eighth of them use ChatGPT. OpenAI confirmed that its infamous AI chatbot now has over one billion weekly active users, a staggering number given that ChatGPT is only three and a half years old. (For reference, that's on par with global Windows users.) Love it or hate it, there's no denying that ChatGPT—and generative AI as a whole—is firmly a part of modern life.  While there are surely many paying ChatGPT customers, the vast majority are using it for free. Though it may be exciting for paid users to try out the company's latest and greatest models, the biggest impact happens whenever OpenAI makes features available free of charge. As it happens, next week, free users are getting perhaps the biggest ChatGPT update in years. Free ChatGPT users are getting unlimited text chats Starting next week, you'll no longer hit a wall when simply texting with ChatGPT. OpenAI says that both free and Go users now have unlimited text chats, which should mean you can send as many text-based messages as you want without running into cooldown periods. Of course, the emphasis here is on "texts." There are absolutely still limits on other ChatGPT features, including messages with files and images, as well as Voice mode and image generation. But for users who primarily use ChatGPT with text-based messages, this update should be more than welcome.  
In addition, OpenAI is switching free and Go users to the company's new GPT-5.6 Luna model, which is designed for "cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads." As such, this model likely won't be as capable as OpenAI's more powerful models available to Pro users, but free users aren't totally left in the lurch: OpenAI says there's a new "Think" button that lets you push Luna further for more complex requests. The experience is much changed from the days when users could jump between different models for free, but perhaps the unlimited text chats will make up for it for most users.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
ChatGPT Pro users are getting some new perks tooOpenAI says that Plus and Pro users are also getting some updates. The company says that its GPT-5.6 Sol model now delivers "more focused" responses, and may issue corrections instead of simply agreeing with the user when they're wrong. It also does away with some of the formatting we've come to expect from AI: Your answer may be more succinct in paragraph form, rather than expansive with bullet points. OpenAI says that Sol makes "fewer mistakes" too, but remember: all AI models hallucinate.     There's also a new slider to push the model from "Instant" to higher effort. The idea is to give users a sliding scale of power, rather than have them switch from distinct models. The more intense you push the model, the longer the responses may take, so OpenAI positions the slider as an option for users to tailor the model to their needs: If you need a quick answer, keep the slider towards the less intense side.

title: Here's When Google Assistant Is Leaving Android
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 5, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Didem Mente/Anadolu via Getty Images)
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Google Assistant is officially leaving Android. The company has started contacting existing users with the news.
                                            Google says that it will start removing Google Assistant from Android devices starting Sept. 4, though it will take a few weeks in total.
                                            This deprecation affects Android devices and Wear OS smartwatches, as well as some Android Auto cars.
                                            Google built-in cars, Google TV devices, and Google Home speakers and smart displays can continue using Google Assistant past Sept. 4.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        For the longest time, Google Assistant was the bot to beat. While those of us in the Apple ecosystem have struggled to get Siri to follow our commands, Google Assistant could answer almost any query you had. It led the charge on conversational AI, which let you ask a follow-up without needing to restate the original question in full. I've never been one to rely much on assistants, but I'll admit that I've wished Siri could be a bit more like Google Assistant over the years.Of course, Google Assistant isn't Google's assistant of choice these days. Since March of 2024, the company has let users swap out Google Assistant for Gemini, Google's flagship AI platform. Then, just one year later, the company officially replaced its popular bot with Gemini across its platforms and services. Google didn't outright kill off Google Assistant then and there; you've been able to use it if you wish, but it did say it would require Google Assistant at some point in 2025. 2025 has come and gone, and Google Assistant is still here, but that won't be the case for long.    Google Assistant has an official end-of-life dateAs reported by 9to5Google, Google Assistant will officially begin shutting down on Friday, Sept. 4. The company alerted some Google Assistant users via email, letting them know that Google Assistant is being discontinued, and Gemini, "our next-generation AI-powered assistant," is now the official Android assistant. On that date, Google says it will begin removing access to Google Assistant from devices, though it may take "a few weeks to reach everyone." That means you may still have access to Google Assistant through the third week in September, though you could lose access at any point. 
This Google Assistant end-of-life doesn't just apply to Android smartphones and tablets. Google says it will also revoke its legacy assistant from Wear OS watches, headphones, and Android Auto—at least when the feature is powered by the user's smartphone. Google says that "Google built-in" cars will still be able to use Google Assistant after Sept. 4.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Which devices will Google Assistant still work with?At this time, Google TV devices and Google Home speakers and smart displays still have access to Google Assistant. However, in some cases, it seems you cannot revert back to Google Assistant if you choose to use Gemini on your device.

title: This Is Google Play's First Third-Party App Store
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 10, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Google Play now officially hosts a third-party app store, the first of likely many to come.
                                            Aptoide Games is the platforms first third-party app store. Google started allowing these stores on July 22.
                                            The change stems from an agreement between Epic Games and Google, following years of litigation.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        If you have an Android device, you officially have a new app store to try out—the first of likely many to come. Unless you've dabbled in sideloading before, all of the apps on your smartphone or tablet probably came from the Play Store, Google's own app marketplace, or the official app store of your device's manufacturer, e.g., the Samsung Galaxy store. Starting today, however, you can download this new third-party app store from the Google Play Store.As reported by The Verge, starting today, Aug. 10, you can download the "Aptoide Games" app marketplace on your Android directly through the Play Store. Aptoide isn't necessarily new: The company has operated an unofficial app store that you could sideload on your Android before this change, helpful for accessing apps you couldn't find on Google's official store. But now, you're able to install it on your smartphone like any other app from the Play Store.While today is newsworthy, this development could have happened any time over the past two and a half weeks. Google has actually allowed developers to create and distribute third-party app stores on the Play Store since July 22. That decision wasn't really Google's, however, as the company would likely prefer keeping the Play Store as the only official app marketplace available to most Android users. Instead, the change in policy is the result of an agreement between Google and Epic Games, following years of litigation. Epic Games, maker of Fortnite, has long fought both Google and Apple in court, claiming the companies had unfair controls over app marketplaces.   
While not all of Epic Games' suits have been fruitful, the company has certainly succeeded: A judge found Google had an illegal monopoly over Android applications and needed to open up its platform to third-party options. Google fought the ruling, then tried to compromise with Epic Games to allow for third-party app stores—just not through the Play Store. The company rather abruptly changed course, however, and agreed to host third-party app stores on the Play Store. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
While app marketplaces like Aptoide Games are now allowed on the Play Store, they have to operate under some specific rules set out by Google, especially as it pertains to security, privacy, and user safety. They can distribute their own apps, as well as apps found on the Play Store, but they must pay Google certain fees to maintain the overall integrity of the platform. Aptoide might be the first, but it won't be the last. Expect Epic Games to launch its own app store imminently, seeing as it was the company leading this charge in the first place. But more app marketplaces will likely follow suit.

title: Watch Out for These Fake Fraud Alerts From Apple and Amazon
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 11, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Zooey Liao/Lifehacker/Getty Images
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        If you get a security pop-up while you're browsing online alerting you to an unauthorized charge attached to one of your accounts, don't panic, and don't act impulsively. Scammers are currently using these alerts to impersonate Apple and Amazon support (and possibly others) to convince people that their accounts have been compromised and need to be verified to prevent further fraudulent activity. Naturally, this is just a ruse designed to gain access to your device or accounts, which will do far more damage than the fake alert itself. How the unauthorized charge scam worksThis campaign, described by Malwarebytes Labs, starts with a browser pop-up that appears on top of Apple's or Amazon's website. The alerts are designed to look like legitimate notifications and state that the user's Apple ID or Amazon account was recently used to make a $149.99 purchase. Targets are urged to call the support number listed—the same on both pop-ups—immediately to prevent further unauthorized activity. The scammer on the other end of the line may try to convince you to download a tool that provides remote access to your device, hand over credentials, or even pay a fee to protect your account. If you Google the number listed in this specific campaign, you'll find a fake Amazon support website ("amazonhelp[dot]support") set up by fraudsters to make the scheme look more legitimate—of course, the real Amazon customer service site is hosted on amazon.com. Other scam hallmarks present here include manufactured urgency, technical jargon, and a dollar amount that's just enough to get your attention but not so high that it seems like an obvious fake. 
Know how to identify a real fraudulent charge notificationFirst things first: no legitimate company will send you security alerts via browser pop-up. If there's an issue with your account, you may receive an in-app notification or an email, though you should always be wary of the latter, as it's also a common vector for scams. To confirm whether these alerts are real, log into your account by going directly to the website or app and check your message history or activity log. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
It's also worth noting that you won't dispute fraudulent charges with customer support over the phone. In fact, you're far more likely to deal with your bank or credit card issuer directly for this, and you may actually get a fraud notification from a financial institution first in the event of a suspicious purchase. Calling a number from a browser pop-up is not the way. Do not give out account information to anyone over the phone unless you have verified the number, such as by clicking through the company's app, and initiated the call yourself. Finally, these fake pop-ups may be the result of malicious ads, browser redirects, or compromised sites, all of which are used in phishing campaigns. If you're served one, exit the tab immediately and do not click or engage with it further.

title: Why Microsoft Patch Tuesday Updates Suddenly Have So Many More Fixes
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 12, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Credit: Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        If you're a Windows user, you've hopefully installed regular Patch Tuesday updates from Microsoft, which address critical security vulnerabilities across the company's software. The last few months' worth of fixes have been especially important, as they've included a record number of bugs and a swath of zero-days that have been actively exploited or publicly disclosed. The August Patch Tuesday release this week is no different: The update fixes 400 flaws, including three zero-days. Compare that to March, when Microsoft issued patches for just 83 bugs in total (two of which were publicly disclosed zero-days). The seemingly sudden uptick in vulnerabilities and security fixes is due, in large part, to AI. AI is creating vulnerabilities (and discovering them)AI is playing both sides of the field when it comes to security. Threat actors are using AI to develop and deploy hacking tools more quickly and at scale, so more flaws may be more exploitable than before. This forces tech companies to respond more quickly as well. As ZDNET notes, companies that patch vulnerabilities during regular update cycles (like Patch Tuesday) now have to rush to address bugs sooner and may begin to shorten the time between updates, as Apple did earlier this summer.  
While AI is helping to exploit vulnerabilities, it is also finding them so they can be fixed. Last month, Microsoft announced that AI has allowed its engineering teams to find and analyze a larger volume of potential flaws before they can be exploited. (The company noted that this also directly contributes to the increase in security updates included in Patch Tuesday). Google, too, is using AI to discover, triage, and fix security flaws in Chrome. It's worth noting that while AI is good at identifying vulnerabilities, it is far less effective at actually patching them—and may introduce more bugs along the way. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
As always, update your Windows device ASAPWindows users should ensure security updates are installed as soon as they're available to minimize the risk of active exploits. Patch Tuesday is released around 10 a.m. on the second Tuesday of the month, and you should receive them automatically. However, you can check the status under Start > Settings > Windows Update > Check for Windows updates.As BleepingComputer reports, the August security update addresses flaws across the following categories: 176 elevation-of-privilege vulnerabilities, 11 security feature bypass vulnerabilities, 110 remote-code-execution vulnerabilities, 86 information disclosure vulnerabilities, 21 spoofing vulnerabilities, and 12 denial-of-service vulnerabilities. Forty-two of the bugs are rated "critical" and include remote code execution and elevation of privilege flaws.

title: Six New Features Coming to the Pixel Watch 5
description:
We may earn a commission from links on this page.
    
        
        At first glance, you might think Google's new Pixel Watch 5 was actually the P
body:
We may earn a commission from links on this page.
    
        
        At first glance, you might think Google's new Pixel Watch 5 was actually the Pixel Watch 4. That's because it has the same "Actua 360 display" at an identical 320 PPI with up to 3,000 nits of brightness. And, just like the Pixel Watch 4, you can get the Pixel Watch 5 in either 41mm or 45mm models. If not for the new colors, you might think this year's watch is just like last year's watch. It doesn't help that many of the newest software features that Google announced along with the Pixel Watch 5 are compatible with older watches, too. Things like "Health Guardian," which tracks trends in insulin resistance, blood pressure, and sleep breathing, will be available on Pixel Watch 4 when they launch, just as they will be on Pixel Watch 5. But while the Pixel Watch 5 is a small update to the Pixel Watch 4, it is an update: There are six new features exclusive to the watch that you won't find on older models.  The Pixel Watch 5 comes with a new chipThe Pixel Watch 4 runs the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 chip; the Pixel Watch 5 runs the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated chip. That might not sound like a big difference, and, indeed, we don't have benchmarks at this time to say just how much faster the Pixel Watch 5 is than its predecessor. 
However, according to Google, the Pixel 5's "Accelerated" chip is powering on-device AI features faster than before. That includes Google's "Raise to Talk" feature, which lets you interact with Gemini by raising your wrist. The company says these features on Pixel Watch 5 now process "instantly with low latency," even when you aren't connected to the internet. The chip also powers Gemini Intelligence Proactive Suggestions (Google previously called this Magic Cue). These are new suggestions that automatically appear based on the context of what you're doing: If someone asks you for your flight info, Gemini can use your Pixel Watch 5's chip to dig through your apps to surface that info by presenting it as an option to share with a tap. Google says the Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated chip has 50% more RAM than the previous generation, as well as a 12% CPU boost, which makes the whole chip 20% faster overall.  The Pixel Watch 5 has highly accurate GPS route trackingGoogle has some bold claims for the Pixel Watch 5. Not only does the company claim that its newest watch has the most accurate GPS route tracking of any Pixel Watch (the company says it has double the accuracy of previous generations in the "toughest environments"), Google says its more accurate than Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Garmin Fenix 8 Pro. We'll have to see how true those claims are when reviewers put the watch to the test.To make these leaps in GPS route tracking, Google says it tapped into Google Maps to "trace satellite ray paths through 3D building models." The company also explains how Pixel Watch 5 can connect to weather reference stations around the globe in real time to adjust for local atmospheric conditions. Google claims all these steps improve route precision.   
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
The Pixel Watch 5 has improved sleep trackingWhile Pixel Watch 4 shares many of the new health features Google is rolling out in coming months, the Pixel Watch 5 does win in certain categories. Google says the newest watch has 15% more accurate sleep stage detection, which should improve sleep tracking overall. In addition, your bedtime automation on the Pixel Watch 5 can pause audiobooks automatically when you fall asleep, and there's now a dedicated bedtime watch face.New watch faces and complications on the Pixel Watch 5Google says Pixel Watch 5 comes with two new "stunning" watch faces, as well as 11 new "glanceable" complication styles. The company didn't highlight what those looked like in their press releases, but 9to5Google has images of the faces (Weave and Chronograph). You can also use AI to generate new watch faces if the available options aren't to your liking. Pixel Watch 5 comes in new colorsGoogle says the Watch 5 has three new color options, though only two are available in both sizes. Those include Fog, Olive, and Canyon, though the latter is a 41mm exclusive. If you're set on the 45mm model, you could instead choose the Stephen Curry Special Edition, as that model isn't available in 41mm.Breathing emergency detection (EU only)One health feature exclusive to Pixel Watch 5 is "breathing emergency detection." Google says the Pixel Watch 5 can use on-device AI to read its PPG, accelerometer, and barometer sensors all at once, in an effort to detect if you stop breathing. That could be from drug toxicity accidents, pneumonia, or choking. The company says if your watch detects a breathing emergency and you can't respond, it will reach out to emergency services on your behalf, even sharing your live location. This feature is launching in Europe first.

title: You Can (Maybe) Run Meta's Latest AI Model Locally on Your Computer
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 10, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Meta announced Muse Glimmer on Monday, a new open-weight AI model.
                                            Muse Glimmer is designed to run locally on "commercial" Macs and PCs, though the hardware demands are still high.
                                            Your computer should have anywhere from 24GB to 32GB of dedicated RAM in order to run Muse Glimmer locally.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        On Monday, Meta announced its latest AI model: Muse Glimmer. The company isn't necessarily advertising this model as its biggest and best, however. While Meta has plenty to say about Muse Glimmer's performance potential, there are two key selling points for the model in the company's eyes: The fact that it's open-weight, and that it's designed to run locally on "consumer" Macs and PCs—though perhaps not on your computer.What is Muse Glimmer?According ot Meta, Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter AI model optimized for "always-on local agent workflows." What that means is Glimmer is designed to run autonomously directly on your machine, rather than outsourcing that processing to the cloud. Local AI is much more secure than cloud-based, as your data stays within your system. When you tap into cloud servers, you're at the mercy of whichever company owns that network, potentially putting your data in jeopardy.While there are many use cases for a model like Muse Glimmer, Meta is emphasizing its use for agentic AI. AI agents can perform tasks on your behalf and are growing in popularity, as users and developers can ask their agents to do any number of functions. Running agents locally is also quite popular, as evidenced by OpenClaw's infamous year, but the most demanding models also require powerful hardware. If you're working with a laptop, you might not have the energy necessary to run AI agents. 
That's part of Meta's pitch here. The company says Muse Glimmer was trained to balance performance with limited hardware. Meta says it puts Muse Glimmer through three sets of training to achieve this: a "Pre-Training," which trained Muse Glimmer on Muse Spark's outputs; "Mid-Training," which trained the model on more "agent-heavy" data; and "Post-Training," which fine-tuned the model across a number of parameters. Meta says Muse Glimmer can handle end-to-end agentic task completion, multi-step reasoning, recovery when a tool call fails, and multi-model input and reasoning, among other functions. It is also trained on data from over 100 languages. The company says the model performs "strongly for its size class" against many standard LLM benchmarks. 
    
            
            
                                        Credit: Meta
                    
    
While Muse Glimmer isn't as demanding as other models, it likely won't run well on the average laptop. Meta says that a 30-billion parameter model would typically require more than 55GB of memory, but through "quantization techniques," Muse Glimmer can use less than 20GB. When you take its "working memory" into consideration, Muse Glimmer will likely use 24GB or 32GB of memory. If you have a "Pro" MacBook or PC, that might suit you well. But if you're like me, your laptop has 16GB or less of RAM—not quite what Muse Glimmer requires. Still, it's a step forward for local AI use. (For reference, Meta says it tested Muse Glimmer on MacBook M4 Max, M5 Max, and with an RTX-5090 GPU.)Meta says Muse Glimmer is "open," which means Meta released the model's training weights. As such, not only can anyone use the model, but they can tune it as well. If you have specific needs for your AI model, you can tinker with Muse Glimmer to better serve your usage.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
How Muse Glimmer compares to other AI modelsThere are a lot of AI models on the market these days, but Meta only has direct comparisons with two other models: Google's Gemma4-31b and Alibaba's Qwen3.6-27B. According to Meta's benchmarks, Muse Glimmer beats both models in the following 12 tests: MCP Atlas, DeepSearch QA, 𝜏³-banking, WildClawBench, GAIA2, SWE-Bench Pro, Sci Code, Charxiv Reasoning, IFBench, AIME 2026, AA-LCR, and Beam 128K. Gemma4-31b still has the crown in four of the benchmarks, while Qwen3.6-27B leads in eight.Meta didn't provide similar comparisons with models from industry leaders, like OpenAI, DeepSeek, Z.ai, or Moonshot AI. However, Artificial Analysis has a ranking of all open-weight models on the market. As of this article, Muse Glimmer (high) is actually in 18th place. Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 (max) is in the lead, with Z.ai's GLM-5.2 (max) in second, DeepSeek's V4 Flash (max) in third, and Kimi K3 in (low) in fourth. For reference, Gemma4-31b is in 32nd, while Qwen3.6-27B is actually in 17th. There are many variables here, but this leaderboard gives us a quick glance at how Meta's latest model ranks amongst the competition. How to try Muse GlimmerYou can try Muse Glimmer right now by downloading the weights from Hugging Face. Meta says the model will be available in the coming days from apps like Ollama, LM Studio, and Unsloth.

title: Apple TV Just Added These 'Classic' Movies to Its Catalog for Free
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 13, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Gavin Roberts/MacFormat Magazine/Future via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Apple just added 19 "classic" movies to its Apple TV platform for free.
                                            The movies run the gamut, spanning classics from the 80s through the 2010s.
                                            Apple has licensed movies like this in the past, but the promotion didn't last long.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Over the past seven years, Apple TV has slowly become the streaming service to beat. The platform now has a plethora of must-see TV programs, from buzzy hits like Ted Lasso, Severance, and Shrinking to strong sci-fi fare like Foundation and Silo—not to mention Apple Original movies, including Killers of the Flower Moon, F1, and Coda. While the streaming service isn't the first platform that comes to mind for non-Apple content, it does occasionally license shows and movies in addition to its own original programming—including, notably, those old Peanuts specials—and as of today, that licensed catalog just got a bit bigger.   As spotted by 9to5Mac, Apple TV has added 19 movies to its catalog that subscribers can watch for free, without paying a separate rental fee. The selection runs the gamut, featuring films from the 80s, 90s, 2000s, and 2010s and spanning genres and subject matter. Though not all of these movies are exactly awards material, a number of them are considered classics in their own right, from older hits like E.T. and Titanic to recently lauded movies like Arrival. Each of them is free to watch with any Apple TV subscription, and you can find them in the platform's "Great Movies Available Now on Apple TV" section. Apple TV now lets you watch the following movies for freeHere is the complete list of all the movies Apple TV just added to its catalog for free:21 Jump Street
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
A Beautiful MindArrivalThe AviatorThe Bourne IdentityCharlies AngelsE.T.Forgetting Sarah MarshallGone GirlI, RobotLooperThe MartianMission Impossible: Ghost ProtocolThe ProposalThe RookieThe Sixth SenseTitanicZodiacZoolanderIt's unclear how long these movies will remain on Apple TV, or whether Apple plans to add more movies to the mix in the future. As 9to5Mac highlights, it's not the first time Apple has licensed movies in this way, though it has been several years, and previously, Apple has removed the offerings from the platform in short order. All of these movies are available to rent or buy through Apple's digital store too, so if you miss out on the window, you can always pay a rental fee to view them.

            ExperiencePradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise

    Table of Contents
    
        
        The LG 39GX950B-B UltraGear Evo is down to $1,599 from $1,799.99 on Amazon, saving you $200, or about 11%. It's still an expensive gaming monitor, but this is also a fairly unusual display—its 39-inch OLED has a 5K2K resolution, a 21:9 aspect ratio, and a 1500R curve. LG says it is the first 39-inch 5K2K OLED gaming monitor, and its 143 pixels per inch give it noticeably higher pixel density than LG's larger 45-inch 45GX950A-B. That should make text and smaller interface elements look sharper, so the screen makes more sense for someone splitting time between gaming and desktop work.
You also get some flexibility depending on what you play—at its full 5K2K resolution, it runs at up to 165Hz, which is enough for most fast-paced games if your PC can push that many pixels. For competitive shooters, you can switch to a 2560-by-1080 Dual Mode that doubles the refresh rate to 330Hz. You lose a lot of resolution in the process, but someone chasing higher frame rates may prefer that tradeoff. Also, its fast response time keeps motion looking sharp in either mode, and FreeSync Premium Pro and G-SYNC compatibility help reduce tearing.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
As for connectivity, its DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1 connections give newer graphics cards enough bandwidth to take advantage of the monitor’s higher resolutions and refresh rates. There is also USB-C with up to 90 watts of power delivery, so a compatible laptop can handle video, USB accessories, and charging through one connection. That said, variable refresh rate flicker can become noticeable when frame rates change quickly, and its HDR brightness is not always completely accurate. OLED burn-in is another consideration if you spend long hours with static windows, menus, or taskbars on screen, even though LG includes panel-care features and a two-year panel warranty. Console players also get less value from the ultrawide shape because current PlayStation and Xbox consoles do not natively support 21:9 output.
